summary: The comment opposes the lack of protection for minors from explicit online materials and cites scientific literature confirming the harmful effects of pornography on minors. The text discusses the need to tie E-Rate decisions to educational outcomes to ensure that the program supports educational purposes. It cites the relevant federal law (47 U.S.C. § 254(h)(1)(B)) that requires the program to be used primarily for educational purposes. The comment supports extending CIPA to cover third-party-owned devices to ensure children's safety on all devices connected to subsidized internet services. The text discusses the extension of CIPA to third-party devices, requiring either a ban on third-party devices or the implementation of filtering on all network-connected devices to ensure compliance with CIPA requirements. The text also mentions existing E-Rate requirements for educational use and internet safety policies. The claim is an alternative proposal to extend CIPA to third-party devices to address implementation burdens and ensure compliance with CIPA requirements. The comment opposes extending CIPA to third-party-owned devices and requires network-level content filtering to protect minors from accessing harmful content like pornography.
